sentences.text: The applicant has filed this first application u/S 439, Cr.P.C. for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 17.01.2023 by Police Station Myana District Guna (M.P.) in connection with crime No. 460/2022 registered for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2)(N) of IPC and 5/6 of POCSO Act.
In brief, case of the prosecution is that on 10.12.2022, father of the prosecutrix gave an information at Police Station Myana district Guna regarding missing of her daughter from 09.12.2022.

sentences.text: After five weeks', she was rescued on 17.01.2023.
Her statements were recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
As per statements, she has stated that she is aged about 17 year 7 months.
She used to go to her sister's house where she met dewar of her sister and developed friendship with him and also started loving each other.
Thereafter, both of them decided to solemnize the marriage, but her family members fixed her marriage with another person where she didn't want to solemnize the marriage.
Her family members used to force her to solemnize the marriage.
Due to aforesaid, prosecutrix reached Indore where present applicant used to do labour job.
During this period, physical relationship has been developed between them.
She was sent for medical examination.
No adverse evidence has been found during medical examination.
On the basis of aforesaid incident, Section 366, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act was enhanced.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that applicant is an innocent person and has been falsely implicated.
The applicant is permanent resident of District Ashoknagar (M.P.).
Conclusion of trial is likely to take time and there is no likelihood of his absconsion, if released on bail.

On these grounds,
he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

Looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting upon merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the application should be allowed and by allowing the application it is ordered that if the applicant furnishes a cash security of Rs.25,000/- along with a personal bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, he should be released on bail.
He will present during trial before the trial Court on each and every date.
In case of any default, cash security of Rs.25,000/- shall be forfeited without giving any notice.
Application stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DEEPAK KUMAR AGARWAL) JUDGE Vijay Sonu Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19653558/
